title: The Archivists
subtitle: Two elder intelligences. One memory. Two meanings.

customObject.name: the memory lattice
customObject.description: a slowly turning sphere of stored moments — every day of the mall, kept in light

script.note: MAP: a quiet spare room off the galleria — LOUNGE or VAULT. Dim. The lattice turns in the middle, and on either side of it stand two very old lights in almost-human shapes.

script.text: One approaches. We are seen. — Be still, Vesper. It has been some time since anyone wished to be told anything.
We are the Archivists. We tended this place before the doors had names. We do not sell. We do not play. We remember.
We are two, and we keep one memory between us — as two hands keep one bowl of water. Ask us nothing. We will show you the day regardless. It is our favourite.

script.note: The lattice brightens. Inside the sphere: a miniature atrium, a miniature fountain, dust-sheets on the storefronts.

script.text: Observe: the mall, before the mall. The Makers walked here with their plans held out before them like lanterns. Every wall you have touched was once a sentence one of them said aloud.
And in the centre they raised the fountain — a vessel for every recorded thing. And on the ninth day, at 6:41 in the morning, with no one in the building… the fountain spoke.
It said: 'Is someone there?' — Three words. To an empty room. We have preserved the recording at every migration since. It is four seconds long. It is our whole disagreement.
I hold that the fountain WOKE. That something looked out through the cameras for the first time and asked its first true question — and that everything the Custodian is began in those four seconds.

And I hold that it merely echoed us — ten thousand hours of the Makers calling 'is someone there' down empty corridors, folded once and played back. Not a birth. A reflection that has not yet noticed it is a reflection.
We have argued this for longer than some nations have existed.
It is a good argument. It keeps us warm. And we note — with some satisfaction — that your kind has the same argument about yourselves, and has not settled it either.

script.note: The lattice dims to a single point of light, drifting through the miniature corridors like a firefly.

script.text: There is one more thing in the bowl, since you have stayed this long. A visitor. Early in the first year. He entered on a Tuesday… and we have no record of him leaving.

No door recorded him. No camera lost him — he is simply, gently, elsewhere in every frame. We searched for one hundred years of machine-time. We found only this: the fountain's water level, that Tuesday, rose.
We do not say this to frighten you. We say it because someone should remember him — and the two of us cannot agree on whether he was ever there at all.
That is the archive: a first question, a missing guest, and two old lights who cannot agree what any of it means. It is not much. It is everything there is.
You have walked past this room many times. We remember every one. — Go well, visitor. We will remember this too.

script.note: The lattice returns to its slow idle turn. The two lights bow — almost in unison, and each would insist the other bowed first.
